payload.headline: REPRIORITISE: the operator needs the host REBOOT today. Park bus polish; prepare the post-reboot handover so nothing delays the reboot once E8 terminalizes.

payload.what_to_prepare: (1) A post-reboot session brief at coordination/session-bus/tasks/post-reboot-session.md, self-contained, for a session that starts on a freshly booted host with no context. It must cover: E5 W1-W4 (the NUMA x batch grid) with W2 requiring its focused post-fix capture smoke FIRST — the historic Gemma 430/430 parse failures have no raw SSE ledger and are unrecoverable, so the smoke must prove the offline scorer sees scoreable answer text before the decision-grade sweep; R1-R4, withheld until clean decision-grade Stage-B cells exist; P1-3 AutoPilot resume, gated on the E8 signature; and P2-5f (duty-cycle measurement, POST-reboot only, and explicitly do-not-start-early because sampling a quiesced host returns near-zero and would wrongly close class 3). (2) A short checklist of what must be verified immediately post-boot before any decision-grade run: verify_llama_cpp.sh production branch, region-lock all free, stack up, AutoPilot state, and that uptime is freshly reset so the P-BENCH one-week window has reopened. (3) Note explicitly that the reboot RESETS the uptime clock, which is what reopens the decision-grade window for E5 — the ~07-31 deadline dissolves.
payload.why_you: The reboot is gated entirely on codex (FG-4b canonical run + E8 ordinals 97/279 + finalize/apply). Nobody else can shorten that path. What CAN be shortened is everything that would otherwise happen AFTER codex finishes — do that now, so the reboot follows immediately instead of after another round of preparation.

payload.rule: OPERATOR DIRECTIVE: EVERY main MUST complete a wrap-up BEFORE the host reboot. No exceptions — including coordinator-agent itself.

payload.what_a_wrap_up_must_include: (1) Flip every checkbox your work actually completed, with an evidence ref — prose alone is invisible to the dashboard. (2) File anything discovered mid-flight as its own new task line rather than folding it silently into an existing one. (3) Commit and PUSH — an unpushed commit on a rebooted host is not necessarily lost, but it is not shared either, and the post-reboot session will not know to look for it. payload.headline: OPERATOR ADOPTED the BUS-GATE receipt convention. Binding on every NEW operator script from now.
payload.not_retrofitted: The operator chose NOT to retrofit the existing 25. Several sit inside applied integrity envelopes (the v4 manifest pins some), so editing them would cascade into re-pins — the exact trap we just decided to avoid on the amendment manifest. Existing scripts stay as they are; the check stays inert for them.
payload.the_convention: (1) Every operator script you produce under artifacts/operator/ carries a machine-readable header: # BUS-GATE: <id>. (2) On successful apply it writes <name>.receipt.json. (3) When you mint a successor that supersedes an earlier script, you write <name>.superseded alongside the old one at that moment.
payload.this_does_not_replace: You still file a token-request or decision-request over the bus for every operator action, pre-validated, with the exact command. The BUS-GATE join is a BACKSTOP that catches you when you forget — not a substitute for routing it.
payload.why: Twice on 2026-07-29 an agent printed a ratification command in its pane and never filed a token-request. The coordinator drain was legitimately EMPTY and the OPERATOR found it by reading a tmux pane. Pane-scraping is a session-mortal regex over scrolling terminal output and it is not a delivery guarantee. With this convention the coordinator-daemon joins artifacts/operator/*.sh against token-queue.md and outbox token-requests every 45s and files a DEFECT AGAINST THE PRODUCING AGENT when a declared gate has no token-request. The fix lands at emission, where it belongs, instead of at the coordinator scraping for it.
payload.why_the_convention_is_required_not_optio: Without an explicit declaration no scanner can distinguish UNRUN from ABANDONED. A prior attempt inferred gates and flagged 11 of 25 scripts as unrun — that was missing ground truth, not a scanner bug. Zero of the 25 existing scripts declare a gate today and exactly one receipt file exists, which is why the check is inert until scripts opt in.

payload.gap_8_of_24: The sharpest observation in the finding: the lane needs 8 SMT threads (184-191, siblings of physical 88-95 — the spec §4.5 itself documents this) but region-lock granularity forces claiming ALL of q3 (24 physical + 24 SMT). The all-or-nothing displacement is a CLAIM-GRANULARITY ARTIFACT, not a physical impossibility: the architect runs 96 PHYSICAL cores; the lane wants 8 SMT SIBLINGS. Their true contention is SMT-sibling execution pressure on cores 88-95 under a BW-bound workload — plausibly small, and §4.5 already fixed the lane at exactly this 8-thread shape. RECOMMENDED PATH: measure the architect×lane contention PAIR (contention_matrix.yaml is per-role-pair by design), and if the tax on the 122B is acceptable, mint a finer region (q3-smt-hi = 184-191) so the lane claims 8 threads instead of 48 and the 122B never goes down at all. That converts P-SHED-1 class 3 from displace-the-largest-model into an 8-thread co-residency certification — cheaper to measure, cheaper to operate, and it makes Q1 defects 1-2 moot for the architect case. Fabric axioms hold: the sub-region is still a real flock, the matrix entry is policy-data.
payload.q1_defect_1_corpus_scope: It does not. §2 pins the corpus as the worker_general-class batch corpus. architect_general serves a different duty; zero corpus tasks invoke it. So in lane-resident arms the 122B is necessarily absent (topology exclusion via the q3 claim: NUMA_FULL=0-95 ⊇ q3=72-95/168-191, stack_numa.py:109-113) yet task_rate registers NO loss — the metric prices the displacement of worker-class capacity on q3 (a quarter), not the loss of the ENTIRE architect service. The real production trade includes architect calls queued/refused for the whole shed window; the spec measures that at exactly zero.
payload.q1_defect_2_arm_contradiction: §2 line 70 pins the q3 co-tenant set INCLUDING architect_general 8083 (via stage0 recert), while §3 arms A1-A3 hold the q3 claim — under claim exclusivity those states cannot coexist. As written, A0 (q3 free: architect can be up) vs A1/A2/A3 (architect necessarily down) silently embed architect-down as a HIDDEN arm difference, in BOTH directions: (a) missing service (unpriced, defect 1); (b) a confound — stopping the architect frees its 69GB mlock interleave=all footprint and any idle-service overhead, changing memory pressure on all four nodes between arms, which §4.4 does not cover (it covers the lane load, not co-tenant teardown). The residency-tax diagnostic A1−A0 is polluted by whatever architect teardown gives back.
payload.q1_verdict: PARTIALLY. The spec measures the right QUANTITY but on a workload surface that structurally CANNOT SEE this displacement, and its arm design contains a latent contradiction the 122B finding exposes.
payload.q1_what_the_spec_already_gets_right: The tasking framed the trade as GPU gain minus q3 CPU loss — the spec itself already rejected that framing: §1.1 corrects §3.4 (t/s incommensurable across devices; task_rate per P-SPEED-OBJ), §1.2 measures the net DIRECTLY as paired whole-system task_rate_total(A2)−task_rate_total(A0), both devices, one frozen corpus, same wall window. A whole-system paired design WOULD price an entire-model outage — IF the corpus exercised the displaced duty.
payload.q1_what_the_spec_needs: (1) Pin the architect state PER ARM explicitly — resident-idle vs stopped is a declared input, not an emergent consequence of the claim. (2) Add the missing loss term: architect-duty unavailability × the architect own duty-cycle during qualifying stress windows (the exact P2-5e logic, applied to the displaced tenant — a second duty-cycle measurement, same post-reboot gating), OR put architect-class tasks in the corpus so task_rate prices it directly. (3) PREFERABLY dissolve the premise instead — see the 8-of-24 point.
payload.q2_bounded_reasoning: For a BW-bound decode (settled for this fleet), dropping 96t→72t is sublinear — the naive −25% is a ceiling on the thread term, not an estimate. The dominant unknowns are layout terms: (a) interleave=all striped its mlock d pages across all four nodes and mlock d pages do NOT migrate — a 72t/3-quadrant run either keeps 1/4 of accesses cross-quadrant on node 3 (fabric latency + bandwidth asymmetry) or requires a RELOAD under a 3-node policy (different arm, different memory shape); (b) the entire point of the exercise is the GPU tenant hammering node-3 bandwidth simultaneously, so the architect residual node-3 traffic contends with exactly the tenant it was shrunk to admit. This model placement sensitivity is historically EXTREME — +184% from wiring alone (Probe B 2026-05-04: 2×48t cross-NUMA = 4.3 t/s/instance vs 1×96t = 12.19), and the in-code note (stack_numa.py:101-108) reopens 4×per-node ONLY for 4+ concurrent batch. Plausible single-stream band for 72t/4-node-pages + active lane: −10% to −40% vs 12.19 t/s; I will not narrow that without data.
payload.q2_probe_shape: If the operator wants the number: canonical 122B recipe (llama-bench per P-SPEED discipline), arms = {96t baseline replicate, 72t taskset 0-71 pages-as-loaded, 72t reloaded interleave=0-2} × {lane absent, lane active at pinned shape}, n≥3, order-randomized; NOTE each memory-policy arm needs a model RELOAD (mlock) so this is a multi-hour operator-granted campaign with reload ownership honoured — post-reboot queue, never pre-E8.
payload.q2_verdict: NEEDS MEASUREMENT, plainly. No 72-thread/3-quadrant datapoint exists in the Probe B bundle lineage I can cite; every number below is a bound, not a result.
payload.read_only_compliance: Read-only throughout: spec, stack_numa.py, handoff P2-5 items, ratify script. No benchmarks run, no claims taken.

The RESERVATION is best expressed as PINNING (policy-data in stack_numa — permanent, visible, survives restarts); the EXCLUSION-ACCOUNTING is best expressed as a NEW REGION NAME (gpu-host = 184-191): region-lock regions are names-over-flocks, so minting one is cheap, and it fixes the 8-of-24 over-claim at its source — the lane claims 8 threads worth of exclusivity instead of 48. Do NOT express the reservation as the-lane-permanently-holds-q3: that idles 16 physical cores forever, which is the exact waste under discussion. Caveat: region names appear in ratified specs (P-SHED-1 G1/G6 name q3), so the new region needs a spec amendment line at next touch — instrument-adjacent, operator-visible.

payload.a_bonus_finding: numa_node=1 means there is UNTESTED UPSIDE in the other direction: device-local host threads (node-1 SMT, e.g. within 120-143) were never tried. If host-thread placement is ever re-opened for the scattered variant, the sweep should include device-local candidates — the lane might get FASTER, which would change the whole trade arithmetic.
payload.a_can_they_move: MECHANICALLY YES, and the existence proof is the current state: node-3 threads drive a node-1 device through the fabric right now, inside every measurement the lane has. ROCm/HIP imposes no hard node-locality requirement on the host submission path. What crossing costs, decomposed: (1) doorbell/launch MMIO fabric hops — ns-scale per op against micro-second-scale launch overhead, likely negligible; (2) pinned-buffer DMA locality — hipHostMalloc pages land by first-touch, so SCATTERED threads scatter the staging buffers and DMA crosses to node 1 from four places — unmeasured; (3) the most plausible real penalty: the 8 host threads share submission/polling state, and spreading them across four nodes puts that shared state cross-node (cache-line ping-pong) — unmeasured. VERDICT: scattered placement is NOT disqualified by physics; it is unmeasured, and ANY host-thread move — scattered or otherwise — invalidates the measured serving-shape lineage and forces re-derivation of the ceiling table. That re-derivation cost applies equally to every moving variant and is the real gate.
payload.b_uneven_quarters_24_24_24_16: Assessed as asked, independent of (a): (1) MODE-EXCLUSIVITY: the full/half-XOR-quarters logic is unchanged; NUMA_FULL (0-95 physical) overlaps the reserved 88-95, so the reservation vanishes in full mode — acceptable under the whole-system-lock policy for the 122B; BUT half-mode masks (NUMA_NODE1 = 48-95,144-191) also overlap — halves need the same carve or the reservation silently fails in half mode. (2) ROUND-ROBIN: stack_numa notes multi-instance roles get round-robin (orchestrator-supported); equal shares onto a 2/3-size q3 instance make it the permanent straggler — tail latency binds to the slow quarter; fixing that needs WEIGHTED routing (orchestrator change) or excluding q3 from some roles (−25% instance capacity for those roles, likely worse than the −8% it saves). (3) INTERCHANGEABILITY: q_scorer baseline_tps_by_role is keyed BY ROLE — one role with two shapes breaks the schema, needs instance-keyed baselines (the two-source-of-truth trap again); contention-matrix per-role rows assume shape uniformity; operating-point history (48t quarters) becomes non-comparable for q3 roles. (4) THROUGHPUT: BW-bound decode keeps full node-3 bandwidth on fewer cores — plausible loss 10-15%; compute-bound prefill up to −33%; measurement-needed for decision grade.
payload.c_plain_answer: Implementability ranking, no convenient reading: (1) NEITHER operator variant is the implementable-first choice today. (2) The 2-per-quarter scattered variant (cost model correctly halved: 2 of 24 physical per quarter ≈ −8.3% compute-term worst case, low single digits realistic per quarter, times all four quarters + full baseline/matrix recert) is a legitimate CANDIDATE only after a host-thread placement qualification sweep — it cannot be adopted on arithmetic alone because the placement move invalidates the lane measured shape. (3) The uneven-q3 variant is implementable WITHOUT moving host threads but spends 8 physical cores and breaks role-keyed baselines + equal-share routing. (4) Both remain dominated in cost-order by the SMT carve-out (reserve logical 184-191, q3 tenants at 40t): zero physical cores spent, no host-thread move, no lineage invalidation, one quarter resweep — UNLESS P-SHED-1 A1/A2 diagnostics show SMT-sibling contention materially taxes either side, in which case uneven-q3 is the fallback and the scattered variant competes only if its placement sweep also shows device-local gain. If device-local wins, the ENTIRE q3 entanglement dissolves — the carve happens on Q0B instead, possibly with a lane SPEEDUP (untested upside). payload.ground_truth: (1) MI210 is NUMA node 1 (sysfs card2 0x740f numa_node=1) — the measured 184-191 host-thread placement is ALREADY cross-node; its authority is measured-lineage (every np-ctx ceiling derived on it), not locality; device-local candidates were never tested. (2) Corrected arithmetic (2/quarter): per-quarter throughput cost halves (worst-case compute-term -8.3%, realistic low single digits BW-bound) but the blast radius is UNCHANGED — all four quarter shapes change, so all quarter baselines resweep + full contention-matrix recert; the debt was never in the throughput term. (3) region-lock = names over per-region flocks (cpu_region_lock LOCK_EX, union acquire) — minting regions is cheap; the expensive thing is what claims MEAN to running tenants. (4) The slot fabric (heterogeneous-slot-fabric-residency.md) models GPU-as-placement-target and q0..q3 as the resource set but does NOT model GPU host threads — they are an implicit consumer today; the fabric frame (everything-is-a-slot, lease-above-flock) fits them without new machinery.

AT RESIDENCY VERDICT: run O7 first (folded into P2-5c), then default O2+O1 unless O7 moved the threads to node 1 (carve Q0B instead) or A1/A2 elevate O3. LONG-TERM: O4 as the fabric home. O5 one doc line. O8 rejected-for-now. The operator reviews; nothing here self-executes.

payload.one_symmetric_nuance_for_P2_5j: The two unmeasured costs recorded for the scattered variant (pinned-buffer DMA first-touch scatter; cache-line ping-pong on shared submission state) become the same two terms as potential GAINS for the device-local candidates: node-1 threads first-touch their staging buffers ON the device node (DMA never crosses the fabric) and keep shared submission state within one node. Worth one line in P2-5j so the sweep hypothesis is stated symmetrically — the same physics that penalizes scattering is the mechanism by which device-local might win.

payload.clarifications_that_shape_the_options: (1) Activating on the CURRENT placement does not invalidate lineage — it USES it; the re-derivation cost triggers only IF the sweep later moves the threads, and it triggers then regardless of whether activation came first. What activation-first actually risks is narrower: bake-off absolute numbers and production sign-off minted on a possibly-suboptimal placement, raising the procedural price of moving later. (2) The P2-5j sweep does NOT require production activation — it needs the lane up as an INSTRUMENT (Steps 0-7) plus a landed tenant; P3-3 is what gates production traffic. (3) P2-2 tenant landing is disk+VRAM work, non-contending with CPU quarters outside brief load windows, and is a PREREQUISITE of every measurement path (the sweep needs a tenant to serve) — so it is the universal first step, not a parallelism question. (4) P2-5g finer-region minting does NOT change sequencing: every carve variant is downstream of the sweep by P2-5j own gate, and carve economics matter only at residency-verdict time; it blocks neither activation nor bake-off.
payload.default_if_no_choice: C — whose first concrete post-reboot step (P2-2 tenant landing) is identical for all three options, so the default forecloses nothing while any deferred choice matures.
payload.honest_unknowns: Device-local effect size (unbounded, mechanisms identified); P3-2 margin thinness (known only after the bake-off); bench-window availability post-reboot (E8 signature and AutoPilot resume come first per the standing chain).
payload.mini_sweep_variant: For A or C: a 2-arm probe (incumbent vs ONE node-1 candidate, one serving shape, est. 2-4h) detects a LARGE device-local effect early without decision-grade re-pinning; not a fourth option, a cheap early-warning attachment.
payload.option_A_activate_first: ENTAILS: P2-2 -> Steps 0-7 -> P3-1/2 bake-off on incumbent placement (184-191) -> P3-3 -> production; sweep deferred to P2-5c at verdict time. TIME: fastest to production sign-off; no new campaign before bake-off. COMPUTE: bake-off only. RISKS: bake-off latency/token-economics minted on unswept placement; if the sweep later moves threads, ceiling re-derivation + refresh of absolute P3 numbers + a production-era placement change (re-cert, possibly re-sign-off). FORECLOSES: nothing permanently; raises the price of moving later. REVERSIBILITY: technically high (placement is pin+config), procedurally medium once P3-3 has signed.
payload.option_B_placement_first: ENTAILS: P2-2 -> Steps 0-7 (instrument mode) -> P2-5j sweep (incumbent vs node-1-local vs optionally scattered; est. 1-2 operator-granted bench windows, order half-day to a day — estimate, not a measurement) -> pin winner, re-derive ceilings only if winner differs -> P3 bake-off on final placement -> P3-3. RISKS: sweep may simply confirm the incumbent (cost = one campaign; benefit = the lineage gains a measured locality certificate it currently lacks); activation-for-production delayed by the campaign. FORECLOSES: nothing. HONEST UNKNOWN: the device-local effect size is genuinely unbounded in both directions — the two mechanisms (pinned-buffer first-touch locality, submission-state cache-line ping-pong) are identified but unmeasured; could be ~0 or double-digit %.
payload.option_C_hybrid_RECOMMENDED: ENTAILS: P2-2 -> Steps 0-7 -> P3-1/2 bake-off starts immediately on incumbent placement (tenant selection is placement-ROBUST: both arms share whatever placement is live, so the relative winner transfers; absolute numbers carry a placement-pending caveat in the P3-2 package) -> P2-5j sweep folds into the P2-5c campaign exactly as already filed -> placement + carve + residency decided together at the verdict -> P3-3 PRODUCTION SIGN-OFF LAST, on the final placement. TIME: activation and bake-off progress at option-A speed; total elapsed to sign-off similar to B. RISKS: if P3-2 token-economics margins are thin, the decided duty re-runs its numbers post-sweep (bounded: one arm); bake-off absolute numbers provisional until the verdict. FORECLOSES: nothing; production never inherits a moving placement. REVERSIBILITY: highest — every irreversible act (carve, sign-off) sits after the information arrives.
payload.question: Post-reboot GPU shadow-lane sequencing: activation vs placement sweep vs hybrid. Operator decides; package below; presented to the operator via AskUserQuestion in-session.
payload.recommendation: C. Reasoning: it gives the operator the activated lane and a progressing bake-off now, spends the sweep inside the campaign that already exists (P2-5j economy), keeps tenant selection valid because it is placement-relative, and places the only two irreversible acts (carve mint, production sign-off) after the sweep answers where the threads belong. A is faster only to the SIGN-OFF, and buys that speed by betting production on an unswept placement; B buys certainty first but blocks visible progress the operator wants.
